lines.text: …I was walking home from the convenience store. I saw him under the bridge. That’s all. Can I go home now?
Four…? I only knew about… I didn't know there were others. A pharmacist, a councilman, a nurse… and Ishida… no, I mean, the teacher. I don't know any of them. I just found him, that's all…

…That time… he died between ten and eleven? Then… then I have to tell you. I was already there. Around ten-fifty, I heard it — a tiny bell, ringing under the bridge. And then someone walked away along the riverbank, with a dark umbrella. I couldn't see their face… I was too scared. I hid in a bus shelter for almost an hour before I went down. I'm sorry I lied…
Presents: Ink on the Victim’s Palm
…His palm? A 7… and maybe a 3…? I didn't see that. When I found him, I only saw the crane in his mouth. I don't know what numbers would mean. I'm sorry… I really don't.
Presents: The Bell in the Rain

…You know about the bell already? Then… yes. That's what I heard. A tiny, high-pitched bell, like from a charm or a phone strap. And the person walking away with the dark umbrella… I couldn't see anything else, I swear. Please believe me, Detective.

…Seiran Academy. That's… that's my school. But I'm in class 2-A, not 2-B… and I've never seen that page before. But… if it's connected to Seiran, then… then I should tell you the truth. I knew Ishida-sensei. He gave me private maths lessons at his home, because my family can't afford cram school. It's against school rules, so I kept it secret. That night I was going to his house for a lesson… but at 21:40 he texted me: 'Sorry, Yuki. Cancel tonight. Someone from the old days wants to talk.' It felt wrong, so I went toward his house by way of the bridge. Here… look at my phone.
